Every substitution shown algebraically.

(2015), 'Divergence-free smoothed particle hydrodynamics', ACM SIGGRAPH/Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation (SCA '15), 147-155, DOI 10.1145/2786784.2786796, § 3 eq. (5) — the continuity-equation form drho_i/dt = sum_j m_j (v_i - v_j) . grad_i W. Monaghan, J. J. (2005), 'Smoothed particle hydrodynamics', Rep. Prog. Phys. 68 (8), 1703-1759, DOI 10.1088/0034-4885/68/8/R01, § 2.2 — the symmetric SPH variant of the same continuity formula. Both publish the formula verbatim; substituting the two-particle fixture above into eq. (5) reproduces drho_dt = -0.2984155182973038.

independent_reference.source: Cross-anchor against Phase 0's tools/testkit/golden/tables/cubic-spline-kernel.json which independently pins W(q, h) at q in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2} (verified by Phase 0's tools/testkit/golden/reference_implementations/cubic_spline.py generator). Specifically: W(0, 1) = sigma_3d = 0.3183098861837907; W(0.5, 1) = 0.22878523069459955; grad_W_magnitude at q=0.5 = 0.29841551829730373 = |sigma_3d * f'(0.5)| with f'(0.5) = -0.9375. Multiplying the kernel values from the Phase-0 cubic-spline golden by the (m_j, v_rel) factors of the 2-particle fixture reproduces rho_0 and drho_dt_0 exactly; this anchor establishes Phase-1-to-Phase-0 independence of the DFSPH golden from its cubic-spline-kernel building block.
